question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding and shall be granted recall rights to?
answer:
According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association (LUFA) Collective Agreement, recall rights are granted to individuals who had their appointments terminated and Individuals who are Sessional Members.

For individuals whose appointments were terminated, they shall return to the University at the rank they held when their appointments were terminated, with full recognition for years of service at Laurentian. They have up to thirty (30) days to accept such recall offer and shall terminate their alternative employment and take up the offered post, as soon as they are contractually able to do so but in no instance later than six (6) months after accepting the recall offer (page 183).

For Sessional members, they shall have the right to remain on the roster and exercise roster, seniority and establishment rights for any courses they have earned seniority or establishment rights with respect to, or which are substantially similar to courses for which they earned seniority and establishment rights. They shall also have the right to exercise roster, seniority and establishment rights in any Department/School which offers any such courses regardless of whether they earned their seniority and establishment rights in the Department or School now offering such courses (page 183). For the duration of the renewed Collective Agreement, where no other member has establishment rights, establishment rights shall not be specific to the medium, location, and language of course for all members who have earned establishment rights prior to April 30, 2021 (page 183).

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding promotion procedures. if the?
answer:
The Collective Agreement provides that a member is eligible to apply for promotion from the rank of Lecturer to Assistant Professor, Assistant Professor to Associate Professor, and Associate Professor to Full Professor, or to corresponding advancement for the Librarians/Archivists. The application for promotion shall reach the Dean/University Librarian not later than July 2, for decision in that academic year (Article 5.65.1, 5.65.2, and 5.65.3).

The application for promotion must be made on a prescribed form and forwarded to the office of the applicant's Dean/University Librarian, along with all necessary documentation such as an updated curriculum vitae, a list of at least three referees from outside the University qualified to assess the research and creative works of the applicant, and copies of the research and creative works the applicant wishes to have considered in the examination of the application (Article 5.65.4, 5.65.6).

In making recommendations for promotion, the assessment procedure in Article 5.50 – Assessment of a Member’s Performance is to be followed. Recommendations of the assessors shall consider the assessment of the Member's scholarly activity as judged by four external referees, two of which may be nominated by the applicant if they so request (Article 5.65.7 and 5.65.8).

References:
- Collective Agreement 2017-2020, Articles 5.65.1, 5.65.2, 5.65.3, 5.65.4, 5.65.6, 5.65.7, and 5.65.8
- Collective Agreement 2015-2018 (the context provided), Article 5.50

question: What are the rules concerning resignation?
answer:
The rules concerning resignation are as follows:

1. For Academic Staff, a Member may resign effective June 30 or December 30, with at least three (3) month's written notice to the Vice-President, Academic and Provost. All leaves to which a resigning Member would be entitled must be terminated at that date. (Article 5.85.1)

2. Employment may be terminated at any time by mutual written agreement between a Member and the Vice-President, Academic and Provost. (Article 5.85.2)

3. For Faculty Members on a leave of absence at another university, they are deemed to have resigned six (6) months after they receive tenure at that institution. (Article 5.85.3)

4. Professional Staff will provide their supervisor with a minimum of two (2) week’s notice prior to resigning from their position. (Article 5.85.4)

For retirement, the normal retirement date is the first (1st) day of July next following the attainment of age sixty-five (65), unless the Member's sixtieth birthday falls on the first (1st) day of July, in which case the Normal Retirement Date shall coincide with the Member's sixtieth birthday. Early retirement is governed by the regulations of the Laurentian University Pension Plan and Members retired from this University retain certain rights such as library privileges, parking privileges, University facilities, exemption from tuition fees for themselves, and the possibility to be bestowed the title of Professor/Librarian Emeritus upon retirement. (Article 5.90)

question: What does the agreement say about bargaining unit?
answer:
The Laurentian University Faculty Association's collective agreement, as per the documents provided, states that the bargaining unit includes full-time members of the faculty (excluding those on reduced assignments) and sessional (part-time) faculty. However, it explicitly excludes persons employed through the Centre for Continuing Education, persons who teach courses primarily for non-degree credit students, teaching assistants, field consultants in Social Work, clinical teachers in Nursing, technicians, laboratory instructors, clinical or outdoor school instructors, and any other personnel not assigned responsibility for teaching one or more degree credit courses (Collective Agreement 2008-11, p. 215; Collective Agreement 2011-14, p. 204). The agreement also mentions that the bargaining unit was formed through a merger of the full-time faculty and sessional faculty bargaining units (Collective Agreement 2008-11, p. 216; Collective Agreement 2011-14, p. 205).

Reference(s):
- Collective Agreement 2008-11, pp. 215-217
- Collective Agreement 2011-14, pp. 204-206

question: How does the agreement define or describe absence - general?
answer: According to Article 7.20 of the Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement (page 44, Convention collective 2017-2020), an absence in a general context refers to a situation where a member is not available for regular and continuous work to ensure that all university activities, whether scheduled or unscheduled, can be carried out in an orderly manner. Absences should not interfere with assigned and scheduled activities and the harmonious functioning of the department/school (7.20.1-2). Absences from campus affecting teaching duties are governed by specific articles (7.20.3). During certain periods, such as between Labour Day and Spring Convocation, absences of more than one week require permission from the President (7.20.4-5), and members must remain in communication with the President so that it is reasonably possible for the employer to contact them on short notice (7.20.6). The agreement also mentions exceptional cases where the university may recall a member who is on vacation or leave, but only if it's not done arbitrarily or unreasonably (7.20.7).

question: What does the agreement say about rights, responsibilities and?
answer:
The Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement outlines the rights, responsibilities, and duties of academics in various areas. Here are some key points from the context provided:

1. Teaching/Professional Librarianship/Archives Management (Article 2.00): Members have the right to engage in these activities and are expected to participate actively. For members of the regular stream, this is a mandatory responsibility, while for alternate-stream members, it is expected but not always necessary in any given year.

2. Scholarly Activity (Article 2.00): Members have the right to engage in scholarly activities, which are inherent in their status as academics and flow naturally from their positions.

3. University Governance and Administrative Duties (Article 2.00): Members have the right to participate in university governance and administrative duties, and each member is entitled and expected to share in a reasonable amount of these responsibilities.

4. Outside Professional Activities, Service to the Community, Other Paid Activity (Article 2.00): These activities are undertaken voluntarily by the Member.

5. Bilingualism (Article 5.10): The Employer may require bilingualism for certain positions and consider it a desired qualification for specific responsibilities. A Member's performance in both French and English will be taken into consideration in matters such as promotion and tenure.

6. Rights, Responsibilities, and Duties of Academics (Article 5.15): Members have rights, duties, and responsibilities which derive from their positions as teachers/professional librarians and scholars working within the University community. They are expected to participate actively in Teaching/Professional Librarianship/Archives Management, Scholarly Activity, and University Governance and Administrative Duties, although not necessarily in all three in any one given year.

Sources: Collective Agreement 2015-2018, pages 17, 34; Collective Agreement 2002-2005, page 14; Collective Agreement 2017-2020, pages 5, 56.

question: What is stated about vacation?
answer: According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association Collective Agreement 2017-2020 (page 7), Members who have accumulated five full consecutive years of employment at the university are entitled to an additional two days of vacation for each year of employment thereafter, with a maximum entitlement of thirty-five working days. During vacation periods, Members will be paid but there is no remuneration in lieu of vacation if they choose not to take their vacation allowance (page 7). Members are required to take the vacation to which they are entitled and may not accumulate vacation from year to year. The vacation must be taken between Spring Convocation and Labour Day, unless prior permission has been granted by the Dean/University Librarian. In the event of a Member's death, the value of any unused vacation entitlement will be paid to their beneficiary (page 7). Members retiring, resigning or whose limited-term appointment expires but who are unable to take their full vacation entitlement shall be paid vacation pay as specified in paragraphs 7.15.6 (a) to (c) of the agreement (page 7).

question: What are the rules concerning moving expenses?
answer:
According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association (LUFA) Collective Agreement, moving expenses are reimbursed for full-time Members who move from a distance of 100 kilometres or more from their previous location. The Employer will reimburse claims at the rate of 100% to a maximum of $3,000, with official receipts or reasonable facsimiles as proof (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2012-2016, page 45).

Moving expenses include moving, packing, crating, and unpacking of household goods and personal effects; transfer of family by the most economical means of transportation; reasonable living expenses while traveling to Sudbury; and one advance visit for the purpose of securing suitable housing (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2012-2016, page 45).

Moving expenses paid to a new Member will constitute a loan made by the University. This loan will be retired when the Member has completed three years of continuous service with the University, each year being equivalent to one-third of the reimbursement of the loan (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2012-2016, page 45). If the beneficiary leaves the University before completing three years of continuous service for personal or disciplinary reasons, they must reimburse the University for a pro-rated portion of the loan (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2012-2016, page 45).

For employees appointed on a contract of twelve months or less, moving expenses are not normally eligible for reimbursement. However, under special circumstances, the Vice-President, Academic may allow some amount of moving expenses to be reimbursed (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2012-2016, page 45).

Sources:
LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2012-2016, pages 45 and 96-97.

question: According to the agreement, what applies to appointment and renewal?
answer:
Limited Term appointments are appointments that carry no implication of renewal or continuation beyond the stated term (Context: Collective Agreement 2002-2005, page 35). Appointments can be made for urgent needs with exceptions to the procedures, but such agreements shall not be unreasonably withheld (Context: Collective Agreement 2002-2005, page 35). Term appointees may not apply for promotion in the final year of their term appointment (Context: Collective Agreement 2002-2005, page 36). The total duration of limited term appointments is three years, except by agreement of the parties. For Sessional Members, cancellation prior to the commencement of a course can occur only in accordance with cancellation provisions contained in the contract (Context: Collective Agreement 2002-2005, page 47). The contracts issued to Sessional Librarians and Archivists shall identify in reasonable detail the hours during which the work is to be performed. These hours cannot be changed without the consent of the Member (Context: Collective Agreement 2002-2005, page 48).

question: How does the agreement define or describe discipline?
answer:
The Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement defines discipline as a formal measure taken by the Employer against a Member for serious unprofessional behavior, failure to comply with any provisions of the Collective Agreement (excluding minor technical violations), and in cases of gross misconduct or persistent failure to discharge academic responsibility. Discipline shall be just and reasonable, based on the principle of progressive discipline, except in egregious cases (Article 5.75.2). The following are the only forms of discipline which may be taken against a Member:

For a full-time Member:
1. A letter of reprimand, specifying the grounds and adding this reprimand to the personnel file.
2. Suspension with pay, if and only if the Vice-President, Academic and Provost cites the suspension with pay as a disciplinary measure.
3. Suspension without pay.
4. Withholding of an annual increment.
5. Dismissal of a Member.

For a sessional or part-time Member:
1. A letter of reprimand, specifying the grounds and adding this reprimand to the personnel file.
2. Suspension with pay, if and only if the Vice-President, Academic and Provost cites the suspension with pay as a disciplinary measure.
3. Suspension without pay (for Part-Time Clinicians, the reduction in pay shall be computed as the average salary over the previous 4 weeks).
4. Removal of seniority and/or Establishment.
5. Dismissal of a member for Part-time Clinician.

The agreement also specifies that discipline shall be imposed only in compliance with principles of natural justice and due process, ensuring the Member has a fundamental right to know the nature of the allegations against them and the right to respond (Article 5.75.4).

answer: According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association (LUFA) Collective Agreement for the period 2016-2020 (page 37), a pregnant full-time faculty member is entitled to seventeen (17) weeks of Pregnancy Leave. The agreement also states that if the Member is disentitled or disqualified from receiving EI benefits, or if EI ceases to provide coverage for pregnancy benefits or adjusts the amount of benefits, the Employer shall maintain the Member at 100% of her nominal earnings for the period of her leave unless the Member is disqualified or reduced due to fraud or for engaging in alternate employment (section 25.01 c).

question: How is professional development addressed in the collective agreement?
answer:
The Laurentian University Faculty Association (LUFA) collective agreement addresses professional development under Article 10.40 - Professional Development Expenditure. This article outlines provisions for both full-time staff and part-time clinicians.

For full-time professional staff, they are entitled to three (3) professional development days starting July 1, 2023. These days can be requested seven (7) days in advance, and approval will not be unreasonably withheld. Professional Staff will also be required to provide a description of the professional development activities being pursued during the designated days (Source: 10.40.4).

Regarding expenses for professional development, full-time professional staff will receive 100% reimbursement of tuition if the employer requests them to enroll in a course/conference outside the University (Source: 10.40.5).

Part-time clinicians are not explicitly mentioned under Article 10.40, but they have professional development provisions outlined in other articles. For example, part-time clinicians shall submit an annual report within 30 days of completion of their contract (Source: 10.45.1).

Furthermore, the collective agreement includes provisions for health and safety training, accessibility policies, and other training programs that may contribute to professional development (Sources: 10.1, 11.23, 84).

It's important to note that this response only covers aspects of the collective agreement related to the question about professional development. For a comprehensive understanding of the agreement, readers should refer to the full document.

question: According to the agreement, what applies to promotion procedures?
answer: According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement, the promotion procedures are governed by Article 8.04 Assessment – Renewal of probationary appointments, promotions and tenure (pages 12-13). The evaluation of applications shall be based upon an assessment of the member's performance in teaching, scholarly activity, and university, professional and community service as set out in Article 10, Academic Activity, and in addition for promotion, Article 11.04, Rank Criteria (page 12). The nature and scope of past teaching activities shall be taken into account in assessing a member. If the applicant has faced problems in teaching, the assessors will look for evidence that the applicant has recognized the problems, has taken steps to improve, and has made some improvements that are reflected in independent evidence provided by the member (page 12). The assessors shall be flexible in assessing stronger performance in some areas against weaker performance in other areas. However, in no instance shall it recommend tenure for an applicant if teaching performance is judged unsatisfactory or if the applicant is not engaged in scholarly activity (page 12). For promotions, each committee member shall provide a written statement indicating their vote with supporting reasons to the Secretary (page 13). The committee shall issue its reasoned recommendation on renewals, promotions and tenure no later than 15 December (page 13).

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding academic activity?
answer:
The Laurentian University Faculty Association (LUFA) collective agreement outlines specific features of academic responsibilities, primarily under Priority One - A) Part One - Teaching (5.15.4-5.15.8). Members have an obligation to develop and maintain their scholarly competence as teachers within their area of expertise. They are required to inform students about teaching methods and seek approval for substantial changes in instructional methods that involve significant costs or alterations in the established policy (5.15.5).

Once teaching duties have been assigned by the Dean, it is the responsibility of the Member to teach the assigned courses at the designated time and place, reflecting the approved course content consistent with the University calendar (5.15.6). Members are not allowed to delegate their teaching duties, except for occasional guest lectures.

Teaching responsibilities include being available for reasonable consultation with students during office hours, which shall be included in the course syllabus and posted by the Department/School (5.15.6). A Member shall not be required to co-teach a course without their consent (5.15.7).

Members are expected to comply with all properly established regulations of the University, which are not at variance with this Collective Agreement, and participate in the effective operation of the University, including responsibilities for academic counselling, registration, and supervision of examinations as assigned (5.15.8). During examinations, only the head invigilator shall be a faculty Member. The head invigilator is selected randomly from the LUFA full-time faculty membership and serves until all remaining Members have served (5.15.8).

Sources:
Collective Agreement 2011-14, pages 48-49

question: According to the agreement, what applies to renewal and tenure evaluation?
answer:
The Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement for 2011-14 outlines the criteria for renewal and tenure evaluation as follows (Source: Collective Agreement 2011-14 Appendix K):

1. Teaching: Assessment of teaching quality is determined by the method of teaching evaluation mandated by the Collective Agreement. Student evaluations older than five years are not admissible as evidence, and the committee looks for improvements if problems have been encountered (Clauses 5.10.2 (c) (ii), 5.70.9, 5.60.3 (c) (i)).

2. Scholarly activity: A record of satisfactory scholarly activity as defined in Article 5.15 is required, showing progress in independent research or creative activity (Clause 5.60.3 (c) (ii)).

3. University Governance and Administrative Duties: A record of contributions to university governance and administrative duties is expected as set out in Article 5.15 (Clause 5.60.3 (c) (iii)).

The applicant shall identify all specific items according to which the committee will assess their scholarly activity, based on Article 15 criteria (Source: LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020 26). The assessment review forms and the letter are to be reviewed by the Faculty Personnel Committee before being sent to the Vice-President, Academic and Provost (Clause 5.55.25). If the decision on renewal and tenure applications is not communicated to the member by March 1, they are guaranteed employment for the next academic year (Clause 5.55.27).

question: What are the rules concerning vacation?
answer:
The rules concerning vacation for members of the Laurentian University Faculty Association (LUFA) can be found in Article 7.00 – Vacation Leave and Holidays.

Here are some key points from this section of the Collective Agreement:

1. Full-time members shall be entitled to a minimum of three weeks paid vacation per academic year, pro-rated for partial years (Article 7.02).

2. Sessional appointees shall not be entitled to vacation leave (Article 7.03.1).

3. Vacation shall be taken during the summer months of July and August or at other times mutually agreed upon by the member and the employer (Article 7.04).

4. If a full-time member wishes to take vacation leave during the academic year, they must submit their request in writing to the President at least two weeks prior to the commencement of the proposed vacation period (Article 7.05).

5. In the case where a member is required to teach or perform professional duties during their vacation, the member shall be compensated for any loss of vacation time at the rate of one day's salary for each day of such requirement (Article 7.06).

6. Members may carry forward up to two weeks of accrued vacation into the subsequent academic year, provided that they do not have more than four weeks of accrued vacation at any given time (Article 7.14).

Source: Collective Agreement 2015-2018, Laurentian University Faculty Association and University of Sudbury, pages 44-46.

4. The Union shall receive certain information from the Employer each year, including a list of full-time members, teaching workload, sabbatical or leave information, professional allowances, and financial statements (6.12, page 8).

question: What is stated about workplace environment?
answer:
The collective agreement states that the employer recognizes the importance of providing well-designed, safe, and healthy physical working spaces for members (Context: 3.20.2). It also acknowledges that members should play a substantive role in decisions affecting their working environment, particularly offices, classrooms, studios, research and laboratory spaces (Context: 3.20.2). The employer shall establish a budget of $40,000 per year for the provision of furniture, workstations, and equipment according to the recommendations of the Working Space Committee (Context: 3.20.2).

The workplace environment is also expected to comply with the Occupational Health and Safety Act regarding thermal comfort and air quality (Context: first sentence). The employer shall provide individual office space for newly hired members on their start date, and pay all moving expenses to relocate members within the university (Context: first paragraph).

The employer is committed to providing an environment intended to protect the health, safety, and security of employees as they carry out their responsibilities. This commitment is in accordance with the Occupational Health and Safety Act R.S.O 1990 (Context: 3.25.1). The employer also agrees to maintain a Joint Health and Safety Committee which will independently consider matters concerning the health and safety of employees and students (Context: 3.25.1).

Lastly, the employer is expected to provide, in a fair and equitable manner, at least a securable individual office for each full-time member and securable group offices for sessional members, ergonomically appropriate office furniture, appropriate lighting and ventilation, and maintain reasonable levels of working space (Context: additional information).

question: What conditions apply to redundancy?
answer: A workload redundancy can occur in Laurentian University under specific conditions. The reduction of academic personnel shall be known as a workload redundancy, and the employer agrees not to declare such a redundancy if it would result in insufficient academic personnel for that department/school to continue offering viable programs (Source: 10.10.4 Collective Agreement 2008-11). The proposed reductions must be consistent with normal workloads as defined in Article 5.40 – Academic Workload and shall not create an inequitable workload for the affected department/school (Source: 10.10.4 Collective Agreement 2008-11). Additionally, redundancies may only be justified for bona fide academic reasons or insufficient student demand, where the lack of demand is demonstrable over a period of at least three years and future projections do not indicate any appreciable increase in student demand (Source: 10.10.4 Collective Agreement 2008-11). The employer must form a Redundancy Committee consisting of three members chosen by the union, three individuals named by the employer, and the Vice-President, Academic as non-voting Chair to make its final report within sixty days (Source: 10.10.5-7 Collective Agreement 2008-11).

question: How is patents addressed in the collective agreement?
answer:
The Laurentian University Faculty Association (LUFA) Collective Agreement addresses patents through a Committee on Intellectual Property, Patents, and Copyright. This committee is responsible for defining intellectual patents, conducting business related to them, considering strategies for marketing inventions, improvements, or discoveries, and recommending proposals for modifications or changes in the patents articles of the Collective Agreement (LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2016-2020, p. 61; LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2012-2016, p. 56; Collective Agreement 2008-11, p. 119).

Moreover, the committee is also responsible for mediating any disputes arising out of Articles related to patents and copyright (Collective Agreement 2008-11, pp. 119-120). Additionally, each full-time Member's activities related to the creation and dissemination of knowledge are supported by professional expenditures in each contractual year (Collective Agreement 2008-11, p. 120).

question: According to the agreement, what applies to grievance procedure?
answer:
According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement (2017-2020), a grievance procedure applies as follows:

1. Complaint Stage: Before a grievance can be formalized, the union must first give the appropriate administrative decision-maker an opportunity to rectify the complaint. This discussion should take place within 30 working days of the circumstances giving rise to the complaint. If the complaint is not settled, it shall be referred to the President within 21 working days of the response from the decision-maker (Article 23.03, Step 1).

2. Written Grievance: The Union submits a written grievance to the University President within 21 working days of the response at Step 1. The grievance should identify the nature of the grievance, the specific provisions of the Agreement that are alleged to have been violated, and the remedy sought (Article 23.03, Step 2).

3. Meeting: A meeting will be held within 21 working days of the submission of the grievance between the Employer’s representatives, the Union, and the member(s) affected. The Parties shall make reasonable efforts to resolve the grievance, and the Employer’s response shall be given in writing within 21 working days of the meeting (Article 23.03, Step 2).

4. For patents and copyright disputes, a different procedure applies as outlined in Article 6.40.3. This includes steps such as presentation of the grievance to the Vice-President, Academic and Provost, referral to the continuing Committee on Patents and Copyright, and potential arbitration (Article 6.40.3).

5. Professional development expenditures are supported by annual professional expenditures for each full-time Member (Article 6.45.1).

question: What does the agreement say about distance courses?
answer:
The Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement states that the development and/or supervision of a distance or online education course are governed by specific terms and conditions (Article 8.40). The development of a distance education course is considered equivalent to twice the credit value of the course, but may be lesser or up to a maximum of a full workload (Article 8.40.2).

The compensation for developing a distance education course that is not part of a member's normal workload is an overload payment based on the equivalence outlined in Article 8.40.2. If the supervision of a distance education course is not included as part of a normal workload, it shall be paid for as identified in article 4.56 (Rates of Pay for individuals who conduct instruction through distance education delivery modes). The maximum pay shall be the rate of pay of a Sessional Member without establishment as per Article 4.55 (Rates of Pay for Sessional Members with restrictions as per Article 5.40.6 of Article 5.40 – Academic Workload).

The agreement also mentions that benefits are available to full-time members and Master Lecturer Members, including retirement plans, group life insurance, accidental death and dismemberment, dependent group life, extended health care, dental care, long-term disability, and more (Article 8.45.1). Participation in the retirement plan is mandatory for all new full-time faculty members effective their appointment date (Article 8.45.2).

Regarding class cancellations, if a class is cancelled by the University, there shall be no loss of regular earnings for the sessional teacher (not specified in the context provided for distance education courses).

question: What is stated about personnel files?

An inventory of this confidential material, including authorship, date, and general subject matter, will be provided (pages 102, 42). Members may also request a copy of their personnel file excluding confidential material, which shall be provided within five working days at no charge (pages 103, 43). If any false, irrelevant, or unsubstantiated material is found in the personnel file, members have the right to request its removal through the Dean/University Librarian as appropriate (page 103). The agreement also states that there shall be two types of files for members: active files and archival files. Archival files contain material that has been banned for use in subsequent proceedings but is required by the University for matters other than those related to this Collective Agreement (page 102).

question: What does the agreement say about arbitration procedure?
answer:

Moreover, there's an Expedited Med-Arbitration process outlined in Schedule “S” of the agreement. This process includes the following:
1. Parties may be represented by legal counsel for expedited med-arbitration dates.
2. Up to four dates for expedited med-arbitration will be agreed upon each year.
3. At least 60 days prior to each date, the parties will agree on the grievances to be dealt with.
4. Up to three grievances will be heard on each expedited med-arbitration date.
5. Forty-five days prior to each date, a party may request for production of documents from the other party. Disclosure will be provided within fifteen days.
6. Each grievance proceeding to expedited med-arbitration will be heard and determined on the basis of written briefs prepared by the parties as supplemented by brief oral arguments.
7. The parties will exchange written briefs at least fourteen days in advance of the expedited med-arbitration.
8. The written briefs will contain a summary of facts, copies of all documents, a written argument in summary form, and copies of all cases on which the party relies. The briefs will be sent to the med-arbitrator seven days in advance of the med-arbitration date.
9. If a party does not deliver its written brief within the required time or with the content required, the other party may cancel the med-arbitration date at its sole discretion.
10. Any procedural disputes will be resolved by the arbitrator assigned to the med-arbitration date on an expedited basis.
11. Awards arising out of this process are non-precedential and may not be referred to or relied upon by the parties in any other proceedings unless mutually agreed otherwise. Negotiated settlements may or may not be precedential as agreed by the parties.
12. The med-arbitration will be heard by the following arbitrators on a rotational basis: William Kaplan, Sheri Price, Elizabeth McIntyre and Brian Sheehan (Source document name and page number: Context provided).

In the 2015-2018 LUFA collective agreement, members are granted a leave of up to five consecutive working days without loss in pay to make arrangements for and/or attend the funeral in the event of the death of one of their immediate family. (Source: Collective Agreement 2015-2018, page 37).

These provisions can be interpreted as forms of compassionate leave, although they are not explicitly labeled as such in the agreement.

question: According to the agreement, what applies to demonstrated professional?
answer:
According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement (2017-2020), members of the bargaining unit, referred to as academics, have the right and are expected to engage in various activities in a reasonable proportion that varies from individual to individual. These activities include (a) performing teaching duties as assigned according to the collective agreement, (b) research, scholarly, and creative activities, (c) University service, and (d) Professional and community service (Article 10).

For Members of the Regular Stream and Alternate Stream, their responsibilities related to Teaching/Professional Librarianship/Archives Management, Scholarly Activity, and University Governance and Administrative Duties are inherent in their status as academics. They are expected to participate actively in these areas, although not necessarily in all three in any one given year (Article 2).

Members have the right to freedom in teaching, research, scholarship, creative works, professional and representative academic bodies participation, service to the institution and the community, and expressing their opinions about the University, its administration, and the system in which they work. Academic freedom does not confer legal immunity but requires acknowledging the work of others and accepting responsibility for one's own beliefs and utterances (Article 3.10).

The Employer shall not abridge academic freedom on any grounds, including claims of institutional autonomy (Article 3.10.5). Members also have a right to privacy consistent with the traditions of Academic Freedom (Article 3.15).

question: How does the agreement define or describe sabbatical leaves?
answer:
The Collective Agreement defines sabbatical leaves as a form of leave granted to eligible members who have been full-time faculty or librarians at Laurentian University for six consecutive years, holding the rank of Full Professor/Librarian, Associate Professor/Librarian, and Assistant Professor/Librarian at the time of application. Tenure is required at the start of the sabbatical leave (Clauses 7.25.2 a and 7.25.2 of Collective Agreement 2008-11).

Members on sabbatical leave are not normally assigned any formal workload or expected to participate in any formal University activities, except those required by the agreement. They are entitled to suitable office space on campus if they choose to spend part or all of their sabbatical leave on campus (Clause 7.25.1 of Collective Agreement 2008-11). The Employer retains the right to limit the number of leaves granted in keeping with its academic responsibilities (Clause 7.25.2 Eligibility, Clause 22.09 of Collective Agreement 2018-2021).

The compensation for sabbatical leaves coincides with the Collective Agreement in place, and salary, benefits, and other provisions will be adjusted according to any new agreement between the Board and the Association (Clause 22.09 of Collective Agreement 2018-2021). The agreement also outlines the process for granting sabbatical leaves following an approved application procedure (Clause 7.25.2 Eligibility, Clause 7.25.3 Application Procedure of Collective Agreement 2008-11).

question: What is stated about academic workload?
answer:
According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association Collective Agreement 2017-2020 (page 41), the composition of a Member's workload may vary with their discipline and will take into account their capabilities, potential, and university obligations. The maximum normal teaching load per academic year for Teaching Members is two and a half (2 ½) full courses or fifteen (15) credit equivalents in all Faculties (page 41). Professional Librarian and Archivist Members' normal hours of scheduled student contact shall not exceed twelve (12) per week (page 41).

Members on a twelve (12) month limited-term appointment may have a teaching load of three (3) credits above the normal teaching load, but this above-normal teaching load shall be for a maximum of twelve (12) months only (page 41). The banking or owing of teaching credits is permitted in certain cases such as arranging a teaching-reduced or teaching-free term for scholarly activity, total credit value deviating by not more than six (6) credits from the normal maximum teaching load, academic supervision of an individual student, and courses cancelled due to low enrolment (page 41). Members shall not normally be permitted to bank or owe more than six (6) teaching credits at any given time.

Regarding academic workload decisions, only the decision of the Vice-President, Academic and Provost, regarding academic workload as per Article5.40.6 (d) of Article 5.40 – Academic Workload is subject to grievance (page 13). All other academic workload decisions are not subject to grievance unless they involve allegations of violations of academic freedom, significant procedural irregularities or discrimination (page 13-14).

question: What are the rules concerning professional development?
answer:
The Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement provides guidelines for professional development of its members, specifically in relation to academic qualifications and performance assessment. These guidelines can be found in Articles 5.10 (Academic Qualifications Guidelines), 5.15 (Rights, Responsibilities and Duties of Academics), and 5.50 (Assessment of a Member's Performance).

1. Academic Qualifications: The qualifications for appointment or promotion to different ranks are specified in Article 5.10.2. For example, for the rank of Lecturer, a Master's degree or equivalent is required. For Assistant Professor, a Doctoral degree is necessary, along with satisfactory performance and evidence of scholarly activity over a five-year period. For Associate Professor, a Doctoral degree is required, along with teaching quality evaluation, evidence of scholarly activity, and at least five years of full-time teaching or relevant professional experience. (Source: Page 25)

2. Teaching Evaluations: Members are expected to maintain their teaching dossiers annually, containing course syllabus, student evaluations, and other relevant material. The Vice-President, Academic and Provost communicates the decision on the request prior to the planned date of the course evaluation. (Source: Page 47)

3. Assessment Procedures: The applicant submits their academic dossier to the Dean/University Librarian by July 2, who makes it available to the Department/School by September 1. Members of the Department/School can access the applicant's dossier, and the applicant has the right to update it until the assessment is made. (Source: Page 48)

These guidelines aim to promote professional development and ensure fair evaluation of members' performance in academia. However, specific rules may vary depending on the rank and department of the faculty member.

Revenue from Inventions: Any revenue that the Employer may receive from inventions shall be dedicated to academic development and research, with at least 50% of such income designated for academic development and research in the Faculty/Library with which the inventor is affiliated. These funds shall be maintained in a special account, which shall be open to the inspection of the President of the Union or the President of the Union's designate (6.30.10).

4. Sub-contracting Work: The Employer agrees that it shall not enter any agreement to sub-contract work or responsibilities already undertaken or possessed by the Employer and the Members without securing to the Members who may be seconded to or employed by the sub-contractor all the rights, privileges, and benefits accorded to them in this patent Article of the Collective Agreement (6.30.11).

5. Copyright: The Member who is the creator of any work shall retain the copyright therein unless otherwise stated in the agreement. However, the University shall hold copyright to any work produced by Members as part of their normal workload for the University for use in its distance education courses (6.35.1 and 6.35.2).

question: What conditions apply to retirement?
answer:
According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association Collective Agreement (2008-11), the possible retirement dates and early retirement provisions are governed by the terms of the pension plan to which the university belongs (Article 19.01, page 44). The leaves to which a retiring member would be entitled must also terminate at the retirement date.

In case of sickness or disability, leave shall be granted and the case dealt with within the University sickness and disability provisions (Article 2.41-3c, page 48). If a Member refuses to comply with the requirements of the University's sickness and disability provisions, the President may proceed to lay dismissal charges. However, it is a sufficient defence to prevent dismissal if the Member can establish that failure to perform reasonable duties arose from physical or emotional illness (Article 2.41-3d, page 48).

Admission to the Special Voluntary Early Retirement Plan is available for a four-year period, i.e., from July 1, 2008, to June 30, 2012 (Appendix D, Agreement Between The Board of Governors of Laurentian University and Laurentian University Faculty Association, Phased Retirement, page 225). The provisions of this Special Voluntary Early Retirement Plan may be amended and/or extended with the agreement of both the Employer and the Union (Appendix D, Agreement Between The Board of Governors of Laurentian University and Laurentian University Faculty Association, Phased Retirement, page 20).

Regarding phased retirement, a Member will be expected to continue the full range of her/his normal pre-program duties as agreed with the Chair and proportionate to her/his percentage appointment over the three (3) year period (Appendix D, Agreement Between The Board of Governors of Laurentian University and Laurentian University Faculty Association, Phased Retirement, page 226).

question: How does the agreement define or describe moving expenses?
answer:
According to the 2014-2017 Thorneloe-LUFA Collective Agreement (page 66), moving expenses include:

1. Moving, packing, crating, and unpacking of household goods and personal effects (Article 6.50.1a).
2. Transfer of family by the most economical means of transportation (Article 6.50.1b).
3. Reasonable living expenses for the duration of the trip to the new location (Article 6.50.1c).
4. One advance visit for the purpose of securing suitable housing (Article 6.50.1d).

For full-time Members moving from a distance of 100 kilometers or more, as per the LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2012-2016 (page 45), these moving expenses can be reimbursed up to a maximum of $3,000, with the possibility of exceeding this amount in exceptional circumstances.

In addition, according to the Collective Agreement 2011-14 (Article 8.55.2), moving expenses include:

1. Moving, packing, crating and unpacking of household goods and personal effects.
2. Transfer of family by the most economical means of transportation.
3. Reasonable living expenses for the duration of the trip to the new location.
4. One (1) advance visit for the purpose of securing suitable housing. The newly appointed Members may be accompanied by their spouse in this instance.

In both cases, all claims must be substantiated by official receipts or reasonable facsimiles. The University will reimburse moving expenses at 100% up to specified maximum amounts, with the possibility of exceeding these amounts in exceptional circumstances.

question: What does the agreement say about sabbatical leave?
answer:
The Laurentian University Faculty Association Collective Agreement outlines the conditions for sabbatical leave. To be eligible, a member must have been a full-time faculty member of the university for the past six consecutive years, holding the rank of Full Professor/Librarian, Associate Professor/Librarian, and Assistant Professor/Librarian at the time of application. They must also be tenured at the time their sabbatical leave begins.

During sabbatical leave, members who elect to remain on campus are entitled to suitable office space. If they are required to move their offices, moving and storage expenses will be paid by the employer. The employer may replace members on sabbatical leave when deemed necessary and has the right to limit the number of leaves granted in keeping with its academic responsibilities.

Sabbatical leave is not automatic and shall be granted following an approved application procedure. Time spent on sabbatical leave, study leave, or leave without pay does not count towards sabbatical eligibility. In exceptional circumstances and to attract qualified faculty, the Vice-President, Academic may grant credit towards a sabbatical leave for full-time faculty service at another university.

The agreement also states that under special circumstances, members may apply for sabbatical leave one year prior to the year in which they would normally become eligible. If granted, they will receive a stipend of 80% of their salary. The dean/university librarian may request that members apply for their sabbatical leave after the completion of five years (Sources: Collective Agreement 2017-2020, 2008-11, 2011-14).

question: What is stated about academic personnel committee?
answer:
The Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement (Article 5.55) states that the role of the Faculty Personnel Committee is to review assessments by the Department/School and the Dean/University Librarian on applications for contract renewal, tenure, promotion, and merit increments. The committee's responsibility is to ensure that all applications have been fairly and completely assessed according to the terms of the Collective Agreement. The review shall result in either an endorsement or a refusal to endorse the assessments. The Faculty Personnel Committee shall communicate the result of its review, with comprehensive and substantive reasons, in writing to the Vice-President, Academic and Provost (Page 52).

The Faculty Personnel Committee also has the responsibility to act as a consultant on any other matters as requested by the University or required by the terms of this Collective Agreement. The structure of the committee includes a Faculty Personnel Committee in each Faculty composed of five elected Members plus two alternates, a Dean/University Librarian appointed by the Vice-President, Academic and Provost as the non-voting Chair, with at least two Members being Full Professors from within that Faculty (Page 53).

Additionally, there is a Francophone Faculty Personnel Committee composed of five elected Members plus two alternates. All Members of the Francophone Faculty Personnel Committee must be qualified Francophone Members and two of the six Members must be Full Professors/Librarians and Archivists (Page 53).

question: How does the agreement define or describe family responsibility leave for full-time faculty?
answer:
The Laurentian University Faculty Association (LUFA) collective agreement defines Family Responsibility Leave for full-time faculty as follows:

* Article 25 outlines the provisions for Family Responsibility Leave, which includes Pregnancy Leave and Parental Leave.
* A pregnant Member is entitled to seventeen (17) weeks of Pregnancy Leave (25.01).
* During the period of pregnancy leave, a Member shall receive from the Employer 100% of her nominal salary for the first two (2) weeks, and an amount equal to the difference between the Employment Insurance (EI) benefits received by the Member and 100% of the Member's nominal salary for up to a maximum of fifteen (15) additional weeks, subject to certain conditions.
* Parental Leave is not specifically defined in the provided context but it is mentioned that a Member on pregnancy or parental leave may elect to defer contractual decisions on reappointment or tenure by an equivalent period of time (25.09e).
* The period of a Member's leave shall be included in the calculation of the Member’s length of service for seniority purposes (25.09d).
* If both parents are Members, they may share their paid periods of leave between them and not to exceed the agreed upon threshold (25.09h).
* The provisions of this Article shall be no less than those in the Provincial Employment Standards Act/Legislation and Employment Insurance Act as may be further amended (25.09f).
* Nothing in this Article shall prevent a Member claiming pregnancy or parental leave during a sabbatical leave (25.09g).

question: What is stated about redundancy?
answer:
According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association Collective Agreement (2017-2020), a declaration of redundancy by the Employer can be initiated in two ways: either by Senate resolving to terminate a faculty, department/school or program for reasons other than Financial Exigency (Article 10.10.3(a)), or by the Vice-President, Academic and Provost making a submission that a particular department/school has more members than necessary to fulfill its program and service teaching requirements in light of student demand (Article 10.10.3(b)). Redundancies may be justified only for bona fide academic reasons and/or on the grounds of insufficient student demand, and such lack of demand must be demonstrable over a period of at least three years and projections into the future must not indicate any appreciable increase in this student demand (Article 10.10.4). The Employer agrees that no procedures other than those specified in this Article will be used to deal with redundancies as defined in the agreement (Article 10.10.1).

question: What conditions apply to entitlement terms?
answer:
For Pregnancy Leave, as outlined in section 14.04 of the Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement (pages 36-37), the following conditions apply for entitlement:

1. The Employer supplements Employment Insurance maternity benefits up to 100% of the employee's nominal earnings during Pregnancy Leave, and up to seventeen weeks of leave is granted in accordance with Ontario's Employment Standards Act.

2. To qualify for supplementary unemployment benefits, a member must have completed at least twelve months of continuous full-time active service with the University immediately preceding the Pregnancy Leave.

3. The member must give at least two weeks' written notice to the Employer of the intent to take Pregnancy Leave and the date they intend to commence it.

4. The member must apply for and be in receipt of Employment Insurance maternity benefits, providing the employer with official documentation regarding EI benefits.

5. During Pregnancy Leave, the member continues to accumulate vacation credits and seniority, while Group Benefits and Pension contributions (based on 100% salary) continue during this period.

6. Any period of absence immediately preceding or following such Pregnancy Leave shall be considered a leave of absence without pay, except that the University will continue to pay its share of Group Benefits premiums during a Parental Leave if the employee agrees in writing to pay their share.

7. Immediately following the completion of a Pregnancy Leave and any related leave of absence without pay, the employee is required to return to work for a period equal to the length of the Pregnancy Leave taken (normally 17 weeks). Failure to do so will result in a requirement to repay the Supplemental Unemployment Benefits to the University.

question: What does the agreement say about conditions employment?
answer:
The Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement outlines several conditions of employment, as stated in various articles. Here are some key points:

1. Appointments shall be made only to the ranks and status categories specified in the agreement (5.20.5 and 5.20.6). These include Lecturer, Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, Full Professor, and their library equivalents, as well as limited term, probationary, and tenured positions.

2. Candidates from within the Bargaining Unit shall be entitled to consideration for all advertised posts (5.20.7).

3. All letters of appointment shall follow a standard format outlined in Appendix B – Standard Letter of Employment and Offer of Employment, and no conditions inconsistent with this Collective Agreement should be included (5.20.8). A copy of the letter of appointment will be forwarded to the Union at the same time as it is sent to the applicant.

4. Upon appointment, new Members shall provide copies of their birth certificate, academic degrees, and professional qualifications if required for the position (5.20.9).

5. Teaching load reduction applies to Members appointed at the rank of Lecturer, Assistant Professor, or Associate Professor with three years or less of teaching experience. The teaching load reduction shall be six credits and applies to probationary appointments only in the first year, but can be taken over the first two consecutive years if the Member chooses (5.20.10).

6. Contracts for courses starting in September, January, or May will be issued by August 1, December 1, and March 1, respectively (11.21). Each offer of appointment shall specify the course number(s), the number of credits, terms and conditions of employment including salary, and reference individuals to the collective agreement for benefits, professional development funds, establishment/seniority, deemed hours, and cancellation conditions. A link to the current collective agreement will be sent with every offer of employment (11.22).

7. The purpose of this Collective Agreement is to set forth terms and conditions of employment, promote harmonious relationships between the Parties, facilitate the development of research and teaching for high-quality education, and provide a means for settling disputes that may arise (1.01).

question: According to the agreement, what applies to sabbatical leave?
answer:
According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement for the period 2018-2021 (page 36), members on sabbatical leave will continue to be members of the bargaining unit and enjoy all duties, obligations, rights, and privileges arising therefrom. They may accept paid employment outside the University of Sudbury with prior written permission from the President, provided that such employment is related to the academic purposes for which the sabbatical leave was granted (page 36). Members on sabbatical leave are required to report all non-trivial income for professional services from sources other than the University. This income, along with the sabbatical salary continuation, shall not exceed 100% of the faculty member's normal University income plus reasonable research, travel, and associated expenses (page 36). The period of leave shall be included as credited years of service in determining University pension benefits (page 36). Upon completion of the sabbatical leave, members are required to return to the University for a period equal to the length of the leave taken or to satisfy some other mutually acceptable arrangement with the Employer (page 36). Within 28 calendar days of returning from sabbatical leave, members shall submit a written report of scholastic or professional activities undertaken during the leave, which will become part of their personnel file (page 36). If Members fail to submit this report, sabbatical credit shall not begin to accumulate until January 1 or July 1, whichever is the closest date next following submission of the report (page 42).

References:
- Collective Agreement 2018-2021, pages 36 and 42.
- LUFA-H Collective Agreement 2012-2016, page 32.

question: How is faculty affairs committee (fac) addressed in the collective agreement?
answer:
The Faculty Affairs Committee (FAC) is addressed in the Laurentian University Collective Agreement under Article 8. The purpose of the FAC, as stated in Article 8.01, is to provide the President with reasoned recommendations on applications from members regarding renewal of probationary appointments, promotion, tenure, research or travel fund allocation (when available), sabbatical leave, and other matters that may be referred to the Committee.

The FAC's membership is composed of one tenured member elected by each University Department, two members at large elected from the ranks of tenure or tenure-tracked members, a full-time member-at-large elected to serve as an alternate, the Dean of Arts at Laurentian University (non-voting), the University Registrar or a senior academic administrator (non-voting, who shall be the Chair and Committee Secretary), and all bargaining unit members serving a two-year term (Source: Article 8.02).

The timelines for applications for probationary renewal, promotion, and tenure are specified in Article 8.03. Applications must be filed by September 30 of each year, including all necessary supporting documentation. Members on probationary appointments shall normally begin to undergo a formal tenure evaluation by the FAC in their final year of probationary status. A member may apply for tenure evaluation one year prior to the final year of his/her probation.

The FAC's procedures are outlined in Article 8.06, which includes provisions on quorum, confidentiality, meeting schedule, voting and minutes, and requests by the Union or University to meet with the committee before its first meeting in September (Source: Article 8.06). The FAC is also responsible for issuing its reasoned recommendation on renewals, promotions, and tenure no later than December 15 (Source: Article 8.06).

question: What are the rules concerning recognized and other holidays?
answer:
According to the provided context, the rules concerning recognized and other holidays are as follows:

1. The following days are recognized holidays by Federal or Provincial authorities, and paid time off shall be given to Members (ARTICLE 20.01 and ARTICLE 5.10.1):
   - Founder's Day
   - Good Friday
   - Easter Monday
   - Victoria Day

   - August Civic Holiday
   - Labour Day
   - Thanksgiving Day
   - Christmas Day
   - Boxing Day
   - New Year's Day

3. Members are entitled to a vacation of one (1) month or twenty-three (23) working days after eleven (11) months of service, and annually thereafter. When Members have accumulated five full consecutive years of employment at the University, for each year of employment thereafter they shall be entitled to an additional two days of vacation, up to a maximum entitlement of 33 working days (ARTICLE 3.1).

5. The following holidays may be designated holidays if declared by the Employer: Holy Thursday part-day, Feast Day of St Ignatius Loyola, Christmas recess (Collective Agreement 2018-2021, 16.02).

6. Members are entitled to certain employment-related expenses reimbursement, such as professional/academic development or upgrading, travel expenses for scholarly conferences or seminars, and others (ARTICLE 4.95).

question: What does the collective agreement provide regarding academic freedom?
answer: According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association Collective Agreement 2017-2020 (page 2), academic freedom includes the right, without restriction by prescribed doctrine, to freedom in teaching; freedom in research and scholarship including the right to disseminate and publish the results thereof; freedom to produce and perform creative works; freedom to acquire, preserve, and provide access to documentary material in all formats; freedom to participate in professional and representative academic bodies; freedom to engage in service to the institution and the community; and freedom to express one’s opinion about the University, its administration, and the system in which one works. Academic freedom also entails the right of academic staff to exercise their civil liberties as individuals, including the right to contribute to social change through free expression on matters of public interest, without being censored, impeded, or hindered by the Employer (page 3). The Employer shall not abridge academic freedom on any grounds, including claims of institutional autonomy (page 3). Members have a right to privacy, consistent with the traditions of academic freedom (Article 3.15) and employment equity (Article 3.18) provisions of the agreement.

question: What are the rules concerning voluntary reduced workload?
answer:
The rules concerning voluntary reduced workload at Laurentian University, as outlined in the Collective Agreement 2011-14 (page 133), state that a full-time member of the Bargaining Unit who has at least two years of continuous full-time service may request a temporary reduction in workload up to 50% for a period of twelve months. The request should be made three months in advance to the Department/School and the Dean/University Librarian, with the approval not being unreasonably withheld.

The University can also grant voluntary reduced workloads for periods longer than twelve months and/or renewals of reduction periods, subject to the same approval process. Members on voluntary reduced workload have the right to benefits and contribute to the university's benefits plan according to the Collective Agreement. This includes sick leave, long-term disability coverage, pension plan contributions, life insurance, sabbatical leave entitlements, and remaining members of the Bargaining Unit. Periods of reduced workload are pro-rated for the application of tenure and promotion policies (pages 132-133).

question: What are the rules concerning research and development?
answer: According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association Collective Agreement 2018-2021 (page 17), scholarly activity is defined as research directed towards a contribution to knowledge, participation in academic activities that contribute to the enhancement, creation, and dissemination of knowledge, and research carried out based on traditional/Indigenous knowledge. Members are expected to abide by ethical conduct for research involving humans and to disseminate the results of their work (pages 17-18). Professional development expenses allowable under this agreement include registration fees for scholarly conferences, travel to attend relevant scholarly conferences or seminars, page and reprint charges, professional/academic development or upgrading, hiring part-time assistants in support of research and teaching, and tuition fees (pages 46, 68). The amount of these expenses is limited to $2,450 per contractual year (page 68). In each case, the member must demonstrate that the activity is of good quality and is consistent with the contribution to knowledge (page 51). Scholarly activity does not normally include research directly related to the immediate and normal preparation for teaching activity (page 51). answer:

5. It appears that members teaching at partner institutions may also receive reimbursement for parking costs up to $4.00 per day, but only for scheduled teaching excluding the Laurentian campus (page 32, Collective Agreement 2012-2016).

question: What conditions apply to vacation?
answer:
Conditions for vacation, according to the Collective Agreement 2018-2021 (pages 37-40 and 54-56), are as follows:

1. Every Member who has completed nine (9) months or more of continuous service with the Employer by May 31 in any academic year is entitled to be absent from work during one (1) month or twenty-five (25) working days in each year following such May 31.
   - Members who have completed sixty (60) months or more of continuous service are entitled to an additional two (2) working days for each additional year of employment, up to a maximum entitlement of thirty-five (35) working days.
   - Members with less than nine (9) months of completed continuous service are entitled to vacation in accord with the Employment Standards Act (Ontario).

2. Vacation accrual for Members on sabbatical or study leave:
   - Every Member on a six- or twelve-month sabbatical or study leave will be deemed to have used up during their leave all vacation entitlements accrued prior to the beginning of the leave.
   - Upon return from their leave, and after July 1, these Members will be entitled to one (1) year’s accrued vacation entitlement.

3. Normal Vacation Period:
   - Members are required to take the vacation to which they are entitled. Vacation may not be accumulated from year to year.
   - Members are required to take their vacation between June 1 and Labour Day, unless prior permission has been granted by the President.

4. If Members are unable to complete scheduled duties assigned to them before annual vacation, Members must so report to the President as soon as such becomes known, at least one (1) month in advance of the dates of their intended vacation. Such reporting does not constitute authorization for Members to postpone or cancel the period of their intended annual vacation.

5. Upon termination of employment, Members will be entitled to be paid their vacation accrual as established under this Article and stipulated in their Letter of Appointment.

question: How is promotion procedures addressed in the collective agreement?
answer:
The promotion procedures for Members of the Teaching Faculty at Laurentian University, as outlined in the Collective Agreement, are detailed in Article 5.10 – Academic Qualifications Guidelines, Article 5.15 – Rights, Responsibilities and Duties of Academics, and Article 5.50 – Assessment of a Member's Performance. The specific academic qualifications required for each rank (Lecturer, Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, Full Professor) are also provided in Article 5.10.2.

For promotions, applications should be made on the prescribed application form and forwarded to the office of the applicant's Dean/Director of the Library, along with necessary documentation. The application deadline is September 30th for decision in that Academic Year (5. The application for promotion shall reach the Dean/Director of the Library not later than September 30th, for decision in that Academic Year).

The following documents must be attached to the application for promotion: an updated curriculum vitae, a list of at least three (3) referees from outside the University qualified to assess the research and creative works of the applicant, and a copy of the research and creative works the applicant wishes to have considered in the examination of the application.

In some cases, the Dean/Director of the Library will review each application and determine whether the candidate meets minimum service requirements and has a chance of success that is not low. If the determination is negative, the Dean/Director of the Library will inform the candidate and meet to explain the determination and to suggest what action should be taken to give a future application a reasonable chance of success (6. For promotions to the rank of Full Professor/Librarian, the Dean/Director of the Library will review each application and determine whether the candidate meets minimum service requirements and has a chance of success that is not low).

question: According to the agreement, what applies to appointment and renewal?
answer:
According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association (LUFA) collective agreement, for individuals who had their appointments terminated and are recalled, they shall return to the University at the rank they held when their appointments were terminated, with full recognition for years of service at Laurentian (Schedule "A", Article 4.13). For sessional members, they have the right to remain on the roster, exercise roster, seniority, and establishment rights for any courses they have earned seniority or establishment rights with respect to, or which are substantially similar to courses for which they earned seniority and establishment rights (Schedule "A", Article 4.15).

Upon the completion of negotiations of a first collective agreement for the newly certified Counsellors, the University will enter into a Memorandum of Settlement respecting such negotiations, and attach the resulting agreement to the LUFA Collective Agreement (Schedule "CC"). For appointment and renewal of positions, offers of employment shall specify the course number(s), the number of credits, terms and conditions of employment including salary, and will reference individuals to the collective agreement for benefits, professional development funds, establishment/seniority, deemed hours and cancellation conditions (Schedule "A", Article 11.22).

Regarding appointment decisions for sessional members, all applicants from the roster shall be notified of the appointment decision on or before July 31 for the Fall Term, October 31 for the Winter Term, and February 15 for the Spring/Summer Term (Schedule "A", Article 4.15.19). In the event that an unsuccessful applicant believes that someone else was appointed to the position in violation of the provisions of this Collective Agreement, they may request a review within one month of the notification (Schedule "A", Article 4.15.20).

For cancellation of contracts for sessional members, the agreement of the member must be obtained if the workload of a Sessional Member must be altered or the contract cancelled (Schedule "A", Article 4.25.1). Cancellation Articles shall be used only where there is good reason to believe that enrolment levels may be vulnerable (Schedule "A", Article 4.25.1d). In the event of a cancellation, the Employer shall attempt to find work of equivalent value for which the Sessional Member is qualified and pay a cancellation fee of fifteen percent (15%) of the agreed salary as outlined in the Letter of Appointment (Schedule "A", Article 4.25.1d).

For appointment of candidates from within the Bargaining Unit, they shall be entitled to consideration for all advertised posts (Schedule "A", Article 5.20.7). Letters of appointment shall normally be signed no later than the start of a teaching term in which a Member must first teach, i.e. by September 1, January 1 and May 1 (Schedule "A", Article 5.20.8). New Members shall provide the Vice-President, Academic and Provost copies of their birth certificate, or equivalent document, and certified copies of their academic degrees and, if required for the position, their professional qualifications upon appointment (Schedule "A", Article 5.20.9).

question: What is stated about withdrawal of seniority for?
answer:
Withdrawal of seniority for Sessional Members can occur if their teaching performance is found to be unsatisfactory (Collective Agreement 2008-11, Article 4.40.1). The process begins with an informal investigation that establishes reasonable grounds for a formal procedure. If the decision of the Council, which may differ from that of the Committee, is to revoke seniority rights, the Dean/University Librarian shall advise the Member and the Union in writing, stating reasons (Collective Agreement 2011-14, 4.40.7). The Member then has the right to request an appeal within ten working days of receiving the communication. The appeal shall be heard by a special FPC/FFPC, which consists of the regular FPC/FFPC, augmented by one Sessional Lecturer nominated by the Union who will not vote (Collective Agreement 2011-14, 4.40.7). If the appeal is determined in favor of the Sessional Member and the course has been or comes to be scheduled for the following academic year, the Sessional Member, subject to seniority, shall be assigned to and paid for such a course or courses (Collective Agreement 2011-14, 4.40.8). Withdrawal of Seniority actions must first be initiated by June 1 in order to be effective for the subsequent academic year (Collective Agreement 2011-14, 4.40.9).

answer:
The rules concerning the Redundancy Committee, as outlined in the Laurentian University Faculty Association collective agreement for both the 2017-2020 and 2008-11 periods, are as follows:

1. A Redundancy Committee is formed by the Employer when a state of redundancy is declared (Collective Agreement 2017-2020, 10.10.5; Collective Agreement 2008-11, 10.10.5).

2. The Redundancy Committee shall include three members chosen by the Union, three individuals named by the Employer, and the Vice-President, Academic and Provost as a non-voting Chair (Collective Agreement 2017-2020, 10.10.6; Collective Agreement 2008-11, 10.10.6).

3. The Union shall forward the names of three Members to serve on the Redundancy Committee within ten days of receiving the Employer's notice (Collective Agreement 2017-2020, 10.10.5; Collective Agreement 2008-11, 10.10.5).

4. The Redundancy Committee shall hold its first meeting within fifteen days of receipt by the Union of the Employer's notice (Collective Agreement 2017-2020, 10.10.5; Collective Agreement 2008-11, 10.10.5).

5. Within sixty days of its first meeting, the Redundancy Committee shall make its final report to the Employer (with a copy to the Union) (Collective Agreement 2017-2020, 10.10.7; Collective Agreement 2008-11, 10.10.7).

question: How is probationary copy addressed in the collective agreement?
answer: Probationary appointments are defined as appointments lasting up to a maximum of five (5) years, during which time the Employer and the Member are afforded an opportunity for mutual appraisal. The term limits (three or five) apply whether the term appointments are consecutive or intermittent. Faculty appointed at different ranks will serve varying probationary periods: Lecturer/General Librarian or Assistant Professor/Librarian will serve a five (5) year probationary period, Associate Professor/Librarian and Full Professor/Librarian will serve a three (3) year probationary period. Probation does not imply that the Employer will grant tenure at the end of the probationary period; it does imply that the Employer will give serious consideration to awarding tenure (5.20.18, 5.20.19, 5.20.21). The Collective Agreement is referring to Laurentian University Faculty Association's 2017-2020 agreement, specifically pages 6 and 36.

question: How does the agreement define or describe tuition fee exemption and spousal?
answer:
According to the Laurentian University Faculty Association Collective Agreement, the Tuition Fee Exemption is defined as follows:

1. Eligibility for Tuition Fee Exemption includes all full-time Members as of the effective date of appointment and all retired full-time Members (2014-2017 Thorneloe-LUFA Collective Agreement 65).
2. Spouses and dependants of all full-time Members, and of Members who died while in the full-time employ of the University are also eligible for Tuition Fee Exemption (ibid). Dependents include wife and husband (including common-law relationships), children up to the age of twenty-six (26) years (ibid).
3. Eligibility ceases with the term immediately following the date of termination of employment of a Member, unless otherwise specified in this Agreement (ibid).
4. The conditions for Tuition Fee Exemption include: a student must remain in good standing as defined by the Registrar’s Office; students who are eligible for an exemption from tuition fees are not exempted from the payment of incidental fees; to the extent that a grant is specifically given to defray tuition, a student who receives a grant is not eligible for exemption from tuition fees; and international tuition fees will only be covered up to the rate of domestic tuition fees (ibid).
5. The Employer reserves the right to modify or rescind this policy depending on the development of future government policy that has a bearing on this matter (ibid).
